analysis: Trial succeeded; host validation macro HR@10 was 0.4813 across four categories: Movies_and_TV 0.535, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.505, Electronics 0.385, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.500. Electronics was the weakest category. Allocated GPU time was 345.15 seconds. The malformed pasted diff text was enclosed in an inert string, allowing the active loss implementation to execute. These results establish successful execution, but do not establish improvement over a baseline or identify which design choices helped. Test performance was unavailable.
code_summary: Trains one independent SASRec model per category with seed 42: 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned positional embeddings and item biases, two pre-normalized causal attention blocks, two heads, GELU feed-forward layers, dropout 0.3, and maximum sequence length 100. Training uses sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 2,048 shared uniform negatives, masking target collisions. A balanced token sampler retains every sequence endpoint and samples earlier positions under a 2,048-token cap; the loss equally weights endpoint loss and an estimated per-sequence positional mean. AdamW uses learning rate 0.001, three-epoch warmup, and gradient clipping. Validation selects a single checkpoint per category by HR@10 with NDCG as a tie-breaker. The generated predictor routes by dataset and loads exactly one trained checkpoint per category; no ensemble or separately fitted auxiliary scorer is used.
